_readme: Per-city candidate rosters for SpeedShield expansion. NOT fetched by the app. Pipeline: (1) adjudicate each roster against the city's official list (URLs in sources), (2) python3 scripts/build_city_drafts.py --geocode writes drafts/<city>.geocoded.json with sanity-gated coordinates, (3) tester pin-drops a sample / any flagged rows, (4) verified entries are pasted into MANUAL_CAMERAS in update_cameras.py, which is what goes live. Names follow the app convention 'X and Y: City' (speech stops at the colon). direction_deg -1 = omnidirectional; approaches are recorded for the record even though the alert is omnidirectional (Tempe precedent). Compiled 2026-09-02 from search results only -- every official page was network-blocked from the session; see confidence per entry.

paradise_valley.status: ACTIVE (first US photo-radar town, 1987) - 5 fixed intersections, red light + speed (roadway sensors measure speed on red, amber and green). ADJUDICATED 2026-09-17: the town's Photo Enforcement Program page wording (as surfaced verbatim in the search index) names exactly these five with approaches; the town's 2015-04-29 press release (official PDF) confirms four of them and the 2006 contract-amendment memo (official) confirms Tatum & McDonald. Woz's verbatim fetch of the live page is still owed before go-live. Also on record: an unpublished mobile van and, since 2022-09-01, TWO portable citing units rotating through five school zones -- both publish no locations, so both stay out of scope (Tempe mobile-unit precedent).
sources: https://paradisevalleyaz.gov/DocumentCenter/View/3940/Press-Release-Photo-Enforcement (official, 2015-04-29: Lincoln&Tatum NB/SB + Halo EB/WB, Lincoln&Palo Cristi EB/WB, Lincoln&Mockingbird EB, Tatum&Desert Jewel NB/SB)
